paragraphs: Before the shift, inspect boilers and pressure readings. During operation, monitor temperature curves and adjust loads. Inspect pumps, valves, and piping and listen for unusual sounds. When an alarm sounds, switch to backup equipment and locate leaks. Record meter readings and energy use, then clean the area and hand over operations before the shift ends.

In short, they keep buildings and factories supplied with power and heat. Their work includes monitoring parameters, adjusting loads, conducting inspections, responding to alarms, recording operations, and coordinating maintenance. It requires both thought and hands-on work on the front line of facility operations.
